questions.question: The ratio of present ages of Ram and Sham is 5 : 4. 16 years ago the ratio of their ages was 16 : 11. The sum of their present ages is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Present age ratio = 5 : 4 (Difference = 1 unit); Age ratio 16 years ago = 16 : 11 (Difference = 5 units).

To equalize the age difference, multiply the present ratio by 5 → 25 : 20.

Decrease in ratio units for each person = 25 − 16 = 9 units (or 20 − 11 = 9 units).

This 9-unit decrease corresponds to the 16-year time gap ∴ 9 units = 16 years.

Sum of present age units = 25 + 20 = 45 units.

Total sum = (16 ÷ 9) × 45 = 16 × 5 = 80 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present ratio of Ram : Sham = 5 : 4

Ratio 16 years ago = 16 : 11

**Formula Used:**

Age = Ratio × constant factor (k)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e86f34a342d3b5aebeebafde7e76056ca3f3fa7c26719b647b78d9faaa05f37a.png] 

Let the present ages of Ram and Sham be 5k and 4k respectively.

⇒ Ages 16 years ago = (5k − 16) and (4k − 16)

⇒ According to the question: (5k − 16) ÷ (4k − 16) = 16 ÷ 11

⇒ 11 × (5k − 16) = 16 × (4k − 16)

⇒ 55k − 176 = 64k − 256

⇒ 64k − 55k = 256 − 176

⇒ 9k = 80

Sum of present ages = 5k + 4k = 9k

⇒ Sum = 80 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 80 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two people always remains the same, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Scaling Property

If a ratio is a : b, then multiplying both terms by the same constant x (ax : bx) maintains the same ratio while allowing for comparison with other scaled values.

Future and Past Ages

To find the age after n years, add n to the present age (x + n). To find the age n years ago, subtract n from the present age (x − n).</p

questions.question: Johnny borrows ₹7,000 from a bank at simple interest. After 3 years he pays ₹4,000 to the bank, this amount being entirely adjusted as repayment of part of the principle borrowed. At the end of 5 years from the date of borrowing he pays ₹4,350 to the bank to settle the account. Find the rate of interest.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Amount Paid = ₹4,000 + ₹4,350 = ₹8,350

Total Interest = Total Paid − Principal = 8,350 − 7,000 = ₹1,350

Total Product (Principal × Time) = (7,000 × 3) + (3,000 × 2) = 21,000 + 6,000 = 27,000

Rate (R) = (Total Interest × 100) ÷ Total Product

R = (1,350 × 100) ÷ 27,000 = 5%

**∴ The correct option is C.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Principal (P₁) = ₹7,000

Repayment after 3 years = ₹4,000

New Principal for next 2 years (P₂) = 7,000 − 4,000 = ₹3,000

Total Time = 5 years (3 years + 2 years)

Final Settlement Payment = ₹4,350

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• 
 
 
 
 Year 0
 Year 3
 Year 5
 
 P = ₹7,000
 
 P = ₹3,000
 Repay ₹4,000
 

 Final: ₹4,350

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Payment = 4,000 + 4,350 = ₹8,350

⇒ Total Interest = 8,350 − 7,000 = ₹1,350

⇒ Total Interest = (P₁ × R × T₁)/100 + (P₂ × R × T₂)/100

⇒ 1,350 = (7,000 × R × 3)/100 + (3,000 × R × 2)/100

⇒ 1,350 = 210R + 60R

⇒ 1,350 = 270R

⇒ R = 1,350 ÷ 270

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The correct option is C.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest on Installments

When parts of the principal are repaid, the interest for the subsequent period is calculated only on the remaining balance of the principal.

Effective Principal Method

Total Interest = (Sum of [Principal × Time for each period] × Rate) ÷ 100. This is useful for multiple repayments.

Difference between SI and CI

In Simple Interest, the principal remains constant unless explicitly repaid. In Compound Interest, interest is added to the principal at the end of each period.

questions.question: A shopkeeper claims to sell 450 kg rice at a cost price of ₹40 per kg but uses a weight of 900 grams instead of a one kilogram weight. He makes a profit of ₹2,520 by selling the remaining rice in the black market. The ratio of the black-market price to the original price per kg of rice is:
questions.solution:

Cost price per kg = ₹40

Weight used = 900 grams (instead of 1 kg)

Total rice claimed to be sold = 450 kg

Profit made in the black market = ₹2,520

**Formula used:**

Weight actually sold = (Weight used/1000) × Total rice claimed to be sold

Remaining rice = Total rice - Weight actually sold

Black market price per kg = (Profit / Remaining rice)

**Calculation:**

Weight actually sold = (900/1000) × 450 = 0.9 × 450 = 405 kg

Remaining rice = 450 - 405 = 45 kg

Black market price per kg = Profit / Remaining rice = 2520 / 45

⇒ Black market price per kg = ₹56

Now, the ratio of the black-market price to the original price:

⇒ Ratio = 56 / 40 = 7 / 5

**∴ The correct ratio of the black-market price to the original price is 7:5.**

Distance traveled by 2nd train during "t" = 42 × t

questions.question: How many amino acids are required to make protein?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __20__.

 
• The human body uses just 20 amino acids to make all the proteins it needs to function and grow.
 
• Because amino acids can be arranged in many different combinations, it's possible for your body to make thousands of different kinds of proteins from just the same 20 amino acids.
 
• Although your body can manufacture many of the 20 amino acids necessary to make proteins, it can't make them all.
 
• Those your body can't produce, called the essential amino acids, must come from the foods you eat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/87c1a28e731fadd9279228c1cea2f8e988a3f790bf9ccc89c9b0f02c423b1609.png] ​ 

 
• Non- Essential Amino acid-:

 
 
• Your body can make some of the amino acids necessary for creating new cells either from the remains of old protein cells or from the essential amino acids.
 
• These include glutamic acid, alanine, aspartic acid, and asparagine.
 
• You don't need to get these amino acids from your diet, although some of the foods you consume may contain them.
 
 
 
• Essential Amino Acid:-
 
 
• ​Nine amino acids need to come from the foods you eat since your body can't make them.
 
• These include phenylalanine, methionine, lysine, leucine, isoleucine, threonine, histidine, valine, and tryptophan.
 
• Animal products, including meat, poultry, seafood, and dairy products, contain all of these essential amino acids, while most plant foods, with the exception of quinoa and soybeans, are lacking in one or more of these essential amino acids.
 
• However, eating a variety of different plant foods throughout the day will give you sufficient amounts of all the amino acids.

**∴ The fraction of the number of pages read by Ravish has been read by Soma is (5)/(12)**

questions.question:
In the given figure, A, B, C and D are four points on a circle. AC and BD intersect at point E such that ∠BEC = 130° and ∠ECD = 20°. Find ∠BAC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb1d71405cc888552784e65404b7f2bed51c30d3cfaf69564b916e3915ef4d7e.png]
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem** in **▵CED**, the exterior angle ∠BEC is equal to the sum of interior opposite angles.

∠BEC = ∠ECD + ∠EDC

⇒ 130° = 20° + ∠EDC

⇒ ∠EDC = 110°

Since **∠BAC** and **∠BDC** (same as ∠EDC) are **angles in the same segment** subtended by **arc BC**, they are equal.

∠BAC = ∠BDC = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A **circle** with points **A, B, C, D**. Chords **AC** and **BD** intersect at **E**. ∠BEC = 130° and ∠ECD = 20°.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles on a straight line = 180°; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bd1f9c9f725e39810da860cf3e4cd99796c06b417cf906c224592648fd84012.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the figure, **A-E-C** is a straight line.

⇒ ∠BEC + ∠CED = 180° (Linear Pair)

⇒ 130° + ∠CED = 180°

⇒ ∠CED = 180° − 130° = 50°

⇒ Now in **▵CED**, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠CED + ∠ECD + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ 50° + 20° + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ 70° + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ ∠EDC = 180° − 70° = 110°

⇒ Note that ∠BDC is the same as ∠EDC, so ∠BDC = 110°.

⇒ **∠BAC** and **∠BDC** are subtended by the same **arc BC** in the same **segment**.

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠BDC = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are always equal.

Exterior Angle Property of a Triangle

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two interior opposite angles.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle is called a cyclic quadrilateral, and the sum of its opposite angles is 180°.</p

questions.question: The traffic lights at two different road crossings change after every 54 sec and 76 sec, respectively. If they change simultaneously at 10:15:00 hours, then find the time at which they will change again simultaneously.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the next **simultaneous change**, calculate the **LCM** of the given time intervals.

**LCM** of 54 and 76 = 2052 seconds.

Convert 2052 seconds into minutes: 2052 ÷ 60 = **34 minutes 12 seconds**.

Next time = 10:15:00 + 34 min 12 sec = **10:49:12 hr**.

**∴ The correct answer is 10:49:12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Interval of Light 1 = 54 seconds

Interval of Light 2 = 76 seconds

Initial simultaneous time = 10:15:00 hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4d5de9ca19d6c073c5af67288d717bdaf8f83c2852d65a95b63b2b88c9cecc2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Prime factors** of 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 2 × 3³

⇒ **Prime factors** of 76 = 2 × 2 × 19 = 2² × 19

⇒ **LCM** = 2² × 3³ × 19 = 4 × 27 × 19

⇒ **LCM** = 108 × 19 = 2052 seconds

⇒ Convert to minutes: 2052 ÷ 60 = 34 minutes and (0.2 × 60) seconds

⇒ 2052 seconds = 34 minutes 12 seconds

⇒ Next simultaneous change = 10:15:00 + 00:34:12

⇒ Next simultaneous change = 10:49:12 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 10:49:12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. Used for problems involving **simultaneous events** like bells ringing or lights flashing.

Time Conversion

To convert seconds to minutes, divide by 60. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. 1 hour = 3600 seconds.

HCF and LCM Relationship

For two numbers a and b, Product of numbers (a × b) = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).</p

questions.question: When an article is sold at a profit of 12% and a loss of 12%, the difference between the selling prices of both the deals is Rs.360. The cost price of the article will be:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage difference between 12% **profit** and 12% **loss** = 12% + 12% = 24%.

Given that this 24% difference corresponds to **Rs. 360**.

Using the **unitary method**: 24% → 360.

1% → 360 ÷ 24 = 15.

**Cost Price (CP)** is always 100%.

100% → 15 × 100 = 1500.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit % = 12%, Loss % = 12%, Difference in SP = Rs. 360.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55f7aab9a07cd1bd0ebcf3bde0e8b4bc8c748ed939e4236f04e2f6d77cce4597.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price** be x.

⇒ SP₁ (at 12% profit) = 1.12x.

⇒ SP₂ (at 12% loss) = 0.88x.

⇒ Difference = 1.12x − 0.88x = 0.24x.

⇒ 0.24x = 360.

⇒ x = 360 ÷ 0.24 = 1500.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Calculation

When an object is sold at a **gain** and another scenario results in a **loss**, the total difference in price is the **sum** of the profit and loss percentages applied to the CP.

Cost Price

The **Cost Price (CP)** is always considered as the base (100%) for calculating profit or loss percentages unless stated otherwise.</p

questions.question: The average weight of 8 people increases by (5)/(2) kg if a new person replaces one weighing 50 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the net deviation method for replacement:

Net change in total weight = Number of persons × Increase in average

Net increase = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + Net increase

Weight of new person = 50 + 20 = 70 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of people = 8

Weight of the replaced person = 50 kg

Increase in average weight = 5/2 kg = 2.5 kg

**Formula Used:**

Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + (Total members × Increase in average)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1fb131b8bc1b79cc54cd2f82f27dff20a1398f5b6a9b90285c6369a33798329c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total increase in weight for all 8 people = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg

⇒ The 20 kg total increase is entirely contributed by the incoming new person.

⇒ Weight of new person = Weight of replaced person + Total increase

⇒ Weight of new person = 50 kg + 20 kg

⇒ Weight of new person = 70 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 70 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Replacement in Average

When an item is replaced by a new item causing the average to increase, the value of the new item is calculated as: New Value = Old Value + (Total number of items × Increase in Average).

Weighted Average

The combined average of two mixed groups is given by the formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The exact average of a dataset can be found rapidly by assuming an average value, adding all the individual net deviations, and dividing that sum by the total number of items.

questions.question: If a seven-digit number 42971K2 is divisible by 44, then the value of K is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by **44** if it is divisible by both **4** and **11**.

For divisibility by **4**: Last two digits **K2** must be divisible by 4 → **K** can be 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

For divisibility by **11**: (4+9+1+2) − (2+7+K) = 14 − (9+K) = 5 − K must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

If 5 − K = 0 ⇒ **K = 5** (Check: 52 is div by 4). If we check options, **K = 5** is present.

Wait, checking **K = 7** from options: (4+9+1+2) − (2+7+7) = 16 − 16 = 0. Also 72 is div by 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = **42971K2**, Divisor = **44**.

**Condition:** Divisibility by 44 requires divisibility by **4** and **11**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6c353dcdab6791403b09d145179f4b69a85f1bb3663a68b2cd94d6b50b1373f.png] 

⇒ **Divisibility by 4:** The last two digits **K2** must be divisible by 4. Possible K = 1, 3, 5, 7, 9.

⇒ **Divisibility by 11:** Difference of sums of digits at odd and even places must be 0 or multiple of 11.

⇒ Sum (Odd) = 4 + 9 + 1 + 2 = 16

⇒ Sum (Even) = 2 + 7 + K = 9 + K

⇒ Difference = 16 − (9 + K) = 7 − K

⇒ For difference to be 0: 7 − K = 0 ⇒ **K = 7**.

⇒ Checking **K = 7** in K2 → 72, which is divisible by 4 (18 × 4 = 72).

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the last two digits of the number are divisible by 4 or are both zero.

Divisibility Rule of 11

Subtract the sum of digits in even positions from the sum of digits in odd positions. If the result is 0 or divisible by 11, the number is divisible by 11.

Composite Divisibility

To check divisibility by a composite number **n**, check divisibility by its co-prime factors (e.g., for 44, factors are 4 and 11).</p

questions.question: What is the value of (2)/(3) div (4)/(27)-(1)/(2) times (4)/(5)+(2)/(7) div (10)/(21)?

2/3 ÷ 4/27 - 1/2 × 4/5 + 2/7 ÷ 10/21

**Formula used:**

Division of fractions: a/b ÷ c/d = a/b × d/c

Multiplication of fractions: a/b × c/d = (a × c) / (b × d)

**Calculations:**

First, simplify each term:

2/3 ÷ 4/27 = 2/3 × 27/4 = (2 × 27) / (3 × 4) = 54/12 = 9/2

1/2 × 4/5 = (1 × 4) / (2 × 5) = 4/10 = 2/5

2/7 ÷ 10/21 = 2/7 × 21/10 = (2 × 21) / (7 × 10) = 42/70 = 3/5

Now, substitute these simplified values back into the expression:

9/2 - 2/5 + 3/5

To combine these fractions, find a common denominator, which is 10:

9/2 = 45/10, 2/5 = 4/10, and 3/5 = 6/10

Now, subtract and add the fractions:

(45/10) - (4/10) + (6/10) = (45 - 4 + 6) / 10 = 47/10

**The value of the expression is 47/10 or 4.7.**

Calculate the sum of all frequencies (Σf):

⇒ Σf = 3 + 4 + 6 + 7 = 20

Now, calculate the arithmetic mean:

⇒ Mean = Σfx ÷ Σf

⇒ Mean = 1052 ÷ 20

⇒ Mean = 52.6

Thus, the arithmetic mean of the given frequency distribution is 52.6.

**Explanation of Options:**

⇒ **Option (1) 52.6** is the correct calculated weighted mean.

⇒ **Option (2) 40.95** is incorrect as it is significantly lower than the actual weighted average.

⇒ **Option (3) 50.5** is incorrect as it represents a simple average of the marks without considering their frequencies.

⇒ **Option (4) 56.2** is incorrect due to calculation error.

**∴ The correct answer is 52.6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean for Grouped Data

For grouped frequency distributions, the mean is calculated as x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ, where xᵢ represents the class mark (midpoint) of each class interval.

Assumed Mean Method

A shortcut method to find the mean of large numbers: Mean = A + (Σfᵢdᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ), where A is the assumed mean and dᵢ = xᵢ − A.

Step-Deviation Method

Used when class intervals are of equal size: Mean = A + h × (Σfᵢuᵢ ÷ Σfᵢ), where uᵢ = (xᵢ − A) ÷ h and h is the class width.

• The **online mode** encompasses websites, online platforms, software applications, and mobile applications.
 
• Customers using these third-party online platforms must be clearly informed about the **foreign exchange rate** quoted by the **AD bank**, its validity period, and the **total estimated transaction cost**.

questions.question: The area of a trapezium shaped field is 1720 m², the distance between its parallel sides is 40 m and the length of one of the parallel sides is 48 m. What is the length (in m) of the other parallel side?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of parallel sides = (2 × Area) ÷ Height

⇒ 48 + b = (2 × 1720) ÷ 40

⇒ 48 + b = 3440 ÷ 40 = 86

⇒ b = 86 − 48 = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of trapezium = 1720 m²

Distance between parallel sides (h) = 40 m

Length of one parallel side (a) = 48 m

Let the other parallel side be b.

 

 
• 
 

 b = ?
 a = 48 m
 h = 40 m
 Area = 1720 m²

**Formula Used:**

Area of trapezium = 1/2 × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1720 = 1/2 × (48 + b) × 40

⇒ 1720 = 20 × (48 + b)

⇒ 48 + b = 1720 ÷ 20

⇒ 48 + b = 86

⇒ b = 86 − 48

⇒ b = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Area of a Trapezium

The area is half the product of the sum of parallel sides and the perpendicular distance between them. Formula: A = 1/2 × (a + b) × h

Perimeter of a Trapezium

The sum of all four sides of the trapezium. Perimeter = a + b + c + d, where a and b are the parallel sides, and c and d are the non-parallel sides.

Isosceles Trapezium

A trapezium in which the non-parallel sides are equal in length. The base angles are equal, and its diagonals are also equal in length.

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment connecting the midpoints of the non-parallel sides. Length of median = 1/2 × (a + b).

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **Modal Class** with the maximum frequency: **12** (Class: **6-8**).

Apply **Mode** formula: L + [(f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

Mode = 6 + [(12 − 8) / (24 − 8 − 6)] × 2

Mode = 6 + (4 / 10) × 2 = 6 + 0.8 = **6.8**.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Class intervals and frequencies: **2-4 (10)**, **4-6 (8)**, **6-8 (12)**, **8-10 (6)**, **10-12 (4)**.

**Formula Used:**

Mode = L + [(f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d36984a483a4ed6846c59d0a4af8a08e42aa9fbd7954eb74d1315987256c7e6d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Maximum frequency (f₁) = **12**, which corresponds to class **6-8**.

⇒ Lower limit of modal class (L) = **6**.

⇒ Frequency of class preceding (f₀) = **8**.

⇒ Frequency of class succeeding (f₂) = **6**.

⇒ Class width (h) = 8 − 6 = **2**.

⇒ Mode = 6 + [(12 − 8) / (2 × 12 − 8 − 6)] × 2

⇒ Mode = 6 + [4 / (24 − 14)] × 2

⇒ Mode = 6 + (4 / 10) × 2

⇒ Mode = 6 + 0.4 × 2

⇒ Mode = 6 + 0.8 = **6.8**

**∴ The correct answer is 6.8.**

Empirical Relationship

The relationship between the three measures of central tendency is: **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean**.

Modal Class Definition

The **Modal Class** is the class interval that has the highest frequency in a grouped frequency distribution.

Bimodal Data

A data set is called **Bimodal** if it contains two distinct values or classes that have the highest and equal frequency.</p

questions.question: If sec θ - cosec θ = 0 and θ is an acute angle, then what is the value of sec² θ + cosec² θ ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If **sec θ = cosec θ**, then **θ = 45°** (since sin θ = cos θ only at 45° for acute angles).

Substitute **θ = 45°** in the given expression: sec² 45° + cosec² 45°.

Value = (√2)² + (√2)² = 2 + 2 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** sec θ − cosec θ = 0, where θ is an **acute angle**.

**Formula Used:** sec θ = 1/cos θ | cosec θ = 1/sin θ | tan θ = sin θ/cos θ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ea8f5b5b32850b28f7e5720ed4e47102868ed94967ab5645126694291490093.png] 

⇒ sec θ − cosec θ = 0

⇒ sec θ = cosec θ

⇒ 1/cos θ = 1/sin θ

⇒ sin θ = cos θ

⇒ sin θ / cos θ = 1

⇒ tan θ = 1

⇒ θ = 45°

Now, calculate **sec² θ + cosec² θ**:

⇒ sec² 45° + cosec² 45°

⇒ (√2)² + (√2)²

⇒ 2 + 2 = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Property

Trigonometric functions satisfy **sec θ = cosec (90° − θ)**. If sec α = cosec β, then α + β = 90°.

Square Identities

Fundamental identities: **1 + tan² θ = sec² θ** and **1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ**.

Special Value: 45°

For θ = 45°, sin θ = cos θ = 1/√2 and sec θ = cosec θ = √2.</p
